clue.text: Jupiter!

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Jupiter! (6)': no word defines or builds SATURN; the clue looks cut short in the OCR (perhaps 'Jupiter's father').

clue.text: Hardy partner had wish for carriage

parts.note: Stan Laurel was the comedy partner of Oliver Hardy
to wish is to hope

explanation.surface: Oliver Hardy's comedy partner longed for a carriage of his own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had' joins the two pieces. A stanhope is a light open one-seat carriage named after the clergyman who first had one built.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanhope is a light horse-drawn vehicle with a single seat, a kind of carriage.

clue.text: Assailed an ally when under the influence of drugs

explanation.surface: Someone attacked a friend while high on drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn on someone is to attack them suddenly; to be turned on is also slang for being high on drugs.

clue.text: Talk on the queen ant

parts.note: R, for Regina, is the usual abbreviation for queen
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lecture about the queen ant of a colony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' joins the definition to the wordplay; the queen ant is two pieces, R and ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: To rant is to talk loudly and at length, a kind of angry speech.

clue.text: It must be well off, but was never enough to make one well off

definitions.text: It must be well off, but was never enough to make one well off

parts.words: It must be well off, but was never enough to make one well off
parts.note: the first 'well off' reads the word as FAR plus THING, a thing that is far off; the second says the coin was worth only a quarter of a penny

explanation.surface: A riddle about wealth: something that is distant yet could never make anyone rich.
explanation.walkthrough: The old British coin, a quarter of an old penny, was worth almost nothing; split in two it reads as a far thing, one well off in distance.
explanation.definitionFit: The farthing was the smallest British coin, too small a sum to make anybody wealthy.

clue.text: Measure of current success with a trial run-and note the gallery

parts.note: the amp is the unit in which electric current is measured
a hit is a success
a heat is a preliminary race, a trial run before the final
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A scientist measuring current has success on a trial run and points out the gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' and 'and' are link words between the pieces; 'the' leads into the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre the amphitheatre is the raised curved tier of seats, a gallery.

clue.text: Surely it carries heavier armament than a water cannon

definitions.text: Surely it carries heavier armament than a water cannon

parts.words: Surely it carries heavier armament than a water cannon
parts.note: reads as an armoured fighting vehicle with a big gun, while also hinting at a container that holds water

explanation.surface: A remark comparing riot-control kit with military weaponry.
explanation.walkthrough: The word names both an armoured military vehicle with a heavy gun and a water container, which the water cannon points towards.
explanation.definitionFit: An armoured fighting vehicle with a large gun outguns a water cannon; the same word is a reservoir for water.

clue.text: High-flier who found, we hear, sunny climes too hot for him

definitions.text: High-flier who found, we hear, sunny climes too hot for him

parts.words: High-flier who found, we hear, sunny climes too hot for him
parts.note: the Greek myth of the boy who flew with wax wings too close to the sun, which melted them

explanation.surface: A successful high-flier who found a holiday in the sun too hot to bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' means 'as legend tells': in Greek myth the son of Daedalus flew too near the sun, his wax wings melted and he fell into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical boy flew on wings of wax and feathers until the sun's heat brought him down.

clue.text: Look given by a saucy bird

explanation.surface: A cheeky bird gives someone a glance.
explanation.definitionFit: A gander is a glance in slang, and the male goose, from the saying that what is sauce for the goose is sauce for its mate.

clue.text: The sort of knave the warrant beheaded

indicators.note: a head cut off means the first letter of the word warrant is dropped

explanation.surface: A rogue whose arrest warrant has been cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrant knave' is a stock phrase for an out-and-out rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrant means utter or downright, the word traditionally paired with knave.

clue.text: Manufactured thread, and apparently made it up too

explanation.surface: Someone who makes thread is also accused of telling tall stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And apparently ... too' links the two senses. Spun yarn is a loosely twisted cord used on ships; to spin a yarn is to tell a made-up story.
explanation.definitionFit: Spun yarn is cord twisted from fibres; having spun a yarn is having told a tall story.

clue.text: The settled estate Moses dreamt of

definitions.text: The settled estate Moses dreamt of

parts.words: The settled estate Moses dreamt of
parts.note: reads like legal talk of a property settled on an heir, but means the land God pledged to the Israelites

explanation.surface: Conveyancing language about a property one Moses had his heart set on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settled estate' sounds like a property law term, but here it is the land agreed in advance for the Israelites, which Moses saw but never entered.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaan was the country God pledged to the Israelites, the goal of Moses' journey through the desert.

clue.text: Heard he'd pay attention

indicators.note: signals that the word he'd is to be said aloud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the contraction of he had or he would, spoken as one syllable

explanation.surface: A report that he had paid attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed is to take notice of something, to listen and mind it.

clue.text: Uniform decoration for railway assistant

parts.note: BR stands for British Rail
an aid is a helper or assistant

explanation.surface: A railway worker earns a decoration on his uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' links the definition and the wordplay. BR was British Rail, the UK state railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold or silver cord is sewn onto military and official uniforms as trimming.

clue.text: Sacking southern England was his aim in the 5th century

definitions.text: southern England was his aim in the 5th century

explanation.surface: An invader of the 5th century set out to plunder southern England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacking' looks like plunder, but it is the coarse fabric. The Jutes were a Germanic people who settled Kent and the Isle of Wight in the 5th century.
explanation.definitionFit: Jute fibre is woven into hessian and sacking; a member of the Germanic tribe settled in southern England.

clue.text: What a political speaker takes to beat an opponent

explanation.surface: A politician's speech meant to beat an opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: A speaker in a debating chamber takes the floor; to floor an opponent is to knock them down.

clue.text: It may carry a silver salt, but not solid silver

definitions.text: It may carry a silver salt, but not solid silver

parts.words: It may carry a silver salt, but not solid silver
parts.note: a photographic glass sheet coated with silver salts, and also silver laid thinly over base metal rather than solid

explanation.surface: A dinner table where the silver salt cellar sits on something that is not solid silver.
explanation.walkthrough: Old photographic sheets were coated with silver salts; silver laid over a cheaper metal is not solid silver.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographic sheet carries a light-sensitive silver salt, and electroplated tableware is silver only on the surface.

clue.text: Delinquent whiz-kid?

parts.note: a youngster who is brilliant at sums might be called a child of puzzles, but the phrase means a difficult child

explanation.surface: A gifted youngster who has gone off the rails.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the second reading: a whiz-kid at maths problems, against the real sense of a troublesome youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: A difficult child whose behaviour causes trouble is a delinquent youngster.

clue.text: He takes a chance on fiddling the gas meter

indicators.note: fiddling means tampering with, so the letters of gas meter are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man risks being caught tampering with the gas meter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambler or habitual player of games of chance takes risks.

clue.text: Don't give rice-wine as a memento

parts.note: not giving something away means you hold on to it
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: Advice to hang on to a bottle of rice wine as a souvenir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake is a small item kept in memory of someone, a souvenir.

clue.text: Intensive patient attention can start once the letters are sorted

indicators.note: the letters of can start once are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Nursing care for a patient can begin once the paperwork is in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' looks like correspondence to be sorted; it means the letters of the preceding words.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbroken round-the-clock nursing is the attention given to a seriously ill patient.

clue.text: The Big Bang makes the news

explanation.surface: A headline: the origin of the universe is in the papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big Bang' suggests the start of the universe, but it is a loud noise, like a gun's.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is the sharp noise of an explosion or gunshot, and also an account in the press.

clue.text: Now wait a minute! I'm going to accelerate!

explanation.surface: A driver tells a passenger to wait, then floors it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase asks someone to pause, and warns a passenger to grip tight before speeding up.

clue.text: Is it perpetual bowing that gives him sore back?

definitions.text: Is it perpetual bowing that gives him sore back?

indicators.note: back means the word sore is read from its end to its start

explanation.surface: A question whether constant bowing is the cause of someone's sore back.
explanation.walkthrough: The god of love is always shown with his bow, so 'bowing' is archery rather than bending; 'back' turns 'sore' round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of love, the winged archer, is always pictured with a bow and arrows.

clue.text: Deck for a party by the navy

parts.note: a do is a party
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A ship's deck is got ready for a party thrown by the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' looks like part of a ship, but it is the verb to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck something is to decorate it with ornaments.

clue.text: Cry a little softly

parts.note: wee means small, a little
p, piano, is the music marking for playing softly

explanation.surface: Someone cries quietly for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed tears is to cry.

clue.text: Many are drawn

definitions.meaning: things drawn in a ballot or raffle are chosen by lot

explanation.surface: Lots of people are attracted.
explanation.definitionFit: There are a great many, and tickets or straws taken at random to decide a choice are drawn.

clue.text: One might hear a starter could be served as a pudding

indicators.note: signals that what a race starter could call out is to be said aloud

parts.note: a starter at a race could say go to begin it

explanation.surface: A dinner where a pudding might be served as the starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like the first course of a meal but is the official who starts a race; 'served as a' joins to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk pudding is made with grains of palm starch.

clue.text: The wife who whipped her children and put them to bed

definitions.text: The wife who whipped her children and put them to bed

parts.words: The wife who whipped her children and put them to bed
parts.note: the nursery rhyme of the woman living in a shoe who had so many children she did not know what to do

explanation.surface: A stern mother who beats her children and sends them to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme ends: she gave them some broth without any bread, then whipped them all soundly and put them to bed. 'Wife' is used in its old sense of woman, and is also slang for a spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery rhyme heroine lived in a shoe, and the phrase is also slang for someone's spouse.

clue.text: Female attire from an Italian province

explanation.surface: Women's clothes from a region of Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantua is a loose gown worn by women in the 17th and 18th centuries, and a province in Lombardy.

clue.text: Deny site reserved for shipyards

indicators.note: read as re-served, served up again in a new order

explanation.surface: A site is refused permission, being set aside for shipbuilding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserved' looks like set aside; read as re-served it says the letters are dished up again. 'For' links; the River Tyne area round Newcastle was famous for shipyards.
explanation.definitionFit: The banks of the River Tyne in north-east England were a great shipbuilding area.

clue.text: Does it lead to our entering the ESE?

definitions.text: Does it lead to our entering the ESE?

indicators.note: entering means the word our goes inside the letters of the exam's initials

parts.note: printed ESE, but the wordplay needs CSE, the Certificate of Secondary Education, a former school exam in England

explanation.surface: A question whether a programme of study leads us to sit a school exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed ESE is a slip for CSE, a school-leaving exam in England before 1988: OUR goes inside it, and a programme of study leads up to such an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A series of lessons in a subject prepares a pupil for an exam.
